title: Five raw observations determine the entire 107-bit generator state
status: New exact all-state certificate, independently replayable with standard-library Python
summary: The explicit recurrence allows a global theorem stronger than a collection of decoding tests. Equality of output words becomes a short-vector problem in an integer lattice. Exact dual bounds exclude every nonzero collision at once. The supplied certificate covers all 126  choices of five positions within nine steps; no enumeration of2^107 states and no trust in an LLL implementation is required.
definitions: Let M=2^107−1, A=3^121 moduloM, and b=2^26. States are integers0≤x_i<M with x_{i+1}=Ax_i moduloM; the raw observation is y_i=x_i modulo b. Since M≡1 modulo3, A is invertible moduloM.
For positions0≤p_0<⋯<p_4≤8 put g_j=p_j−p_0 and Λ_p={d∈Z^5:d_j≡A^{g_j}d_0 moduloM forj=1,…,4}. Let D=⌊(M−1)/b⌋=2^81−1.

result.name: Exact raw-state observability
result.statement: For every five-position subset of{0,…,8}, the selected raw words uniquely determine the initial state. Four raw words cannot determine every state. Every supplied integer basis B_p has rows inΛ_p, |det B_p|=M^4, and DΣ_i|(B_p^(−1))_{ij}|<3/8 for each columnj.
result.proof:
The homomorphism Z^5→(Z/MZ)^4 sending d to(d_j−A^{g_j}d_0)_{j=1}^4 is onto: vary the final four coordinates while keeping d_0=0. Its kernelΛ_p therefore has indexM^4. The checker verifies lattice membership of every basis row and determinant magnitudeM^4, proving that its row lattice equalsΛ_p rather than merely a sublattice. It computes the inverse over rational numbers, verifies B_pB_p^(−1)=I, and checks the strict column bounds for all 126 position subsets. These properties alone suffice; the LLL routine used to find the bases is not trusted.

Suppose two states have the same five observed words. At each selected step their state difference is b d_j for an integerd_j with |d_j|≤D. The recurrence implies d_j≡A^{g_j}d_0 moduloM because b is invertible moduloM. Hence d=cB_p for some integer rowc. Each coordinate satisfies |c_j|=|(dB_p^(−1))_j|≤DΣ_i|(B_p^(−1))_{ij}|<3/8<1. Thusc=0, all selected state differences vanish, and invertibility of A takes equality atp_0 back to equality of the initial states. Four words range over at mostb^4=2^104 possibilities, whereas even the nonzero state set has M−1>2^104 elements. Pigeonhole therefore proves four-word impossibility.

The same dual bounds yield a decoder. Write selected states as y_j+bz_j with0≤z_j≤D. Their congruences define an affine lattice v+Λ_p, using v_0=0 and v_j=b^(−1)(A^{g_j}y_0−y_j) moduloM. For z=v+cB_p, each integerc_j lies in the exact interval obtained by applying the corresponding inverse column to the box0≤z≤D. Its width is below3/8, so it contains at most one integer. Round the interval endpoints exactly, reconstruct z and check all state bounds and observations; then reverse A^{p_0}. This is an actual exact decoder, not only an existence result.

example.setup: Use each of the five states0,1,1234567890123456789,⌊M/3⌋ and M−1, and every five-position subset of the first nine raw outputs.
example.calculation: The checker verifies all 126 lattice bases with exact integers and fractions. Its decoder recovers all 630 specified state/pattern fixtures, including boundary states. The largest dual bound is checked as an exact rational number strictly below3/8; its floating display, about0.368314147, is only for reading.
example.conclusion: The universal conclusion comes from the determinant and dual-bound proof. The 630 fixtures separately verify the decoder implementation on concrete inputs.

limits: Raw observations are consecutive generator steps at known positions, with the source recurrence and output convention stated above. Rejected/accepted-output sequences have hidden step counts and require a different theorem. This certificate makes no claim about their six-output threshold.
extension: Certify additional sparse position patterns, derive the smallest alphabet width permitting five-observation recovery, and optimize the rational basis for a low-cost decoder while retaining exactly the same independent determinant/dual-bound checks.

title: Seven and nine raw observations have optimal one- and two-error correction
status: New exact all-state certificate, independently replayable with standard-library Python
summary: The finite-state trajectories define a code over the alphabet of26-bit words. The five-observation theorem controls its minimum Hamming distance without requiring linearity over a field. A puncturing argument then proves that the seven- and nine-word correction lengths cannot be improved for this full state population.
definitions: For5≤n≤9 let C_n={c_n(x):0≤x<M}, where c_n(x)=(y_0,…,y_{n−1}) is the raw trajectory. Hamming distance counts differing words, regardless of the bit distance within a corrupted word.

An arbitrary word corruption replaces one entire26-bit symbol. Unique correction oftcorruptions requires minimum code distance at least2t+1. Erasures at known positions are a different, easier observation model.

result.name: Exact distance and length-optimal correction
result.statement: For5≤n≤9 the minimum distance of C_n is exactlyn−4. Thus seven raw outputs correct one arbitrary word error, and nine correct two. No code representing all M states over this alphabet can correct one error with six words or two errors with eight words.
result.proof:
If two distinct state codewords agreed at five positions in any n≤9, the preceding theorem would make the states equal. They therefore agree in at most four positions, giving distance at leastn−4. Conversely, for any code of minimum distanced, puncturing d−1fixed positions leaves an injective map: otherwise two original words differed only in those positions, contradicting the distance. Hence its population is at mostb^{n−d+1}. Since M>b^4, one has n−d+1≥5, or d≤n−4. This proves equality.

Two Hamming balls of radius t are disjoint when the minimum distance exceeds2t, by the triangle inequality; hence the stated seven- and nine-word codes uniquely correct the stated errors. An explicit decoder enumerates five-position subsets, applies the certified affine-lattice decoder, re-encodes each candidate and retains a state within the permitted Hamming radius. Enough clean positions remain to produce the true candidate, and the distance proof rules out a second one. Finally any code correcting t arbitrary errors has distance at least2t+1. Puncturing2t positions must be injective, giving M≤b^{n−2t}; sinceM>b^4, necessarily n≥5+2t. This proves the requested length lower bounds without a linear-code assumption.

example.setup: Start at x=1234567890123456789. In its first seven raw words replace position2 by that word plus12345 modulo b. In its first nine words instead corrupt positions1 and7 by offsets54321 and98765 modulo b.
example.calculation: The exact subset decoder returns the original state in both cases. The verification report retains all original and corrupted words. A word can be altered in many bits and still counts as one corruption in this model.
example.conclusion: The finite decoder tests instantiate a globally proved distance theorem, and the puncturing bound proves that shorter full-population codes cannot have the same correction guarantee.

limits: This is a coding theorem for the stated deterministic raw trajectories. It does not assert cryptographic unpredictability, statistical randomness or a correction guarantee when output positions are hidden by rejection sampling.
extension: Study mixed errors and erasures: the same distance gives correction whenever2t+e<n−4. Implement a decoder that uses known erasure locations first, then prove exact failure/refusal conditions for inconsistent observations.
